A PhD in Philosophy or a related field is required at time of appointment.

jobs.description: The University of Toronto Artificial Consciousness Initiative (ACI) is a three-year pilot project advancing foundational research connecting artificial intelligence and consciousness. The project is led by Andrew Y. Lee, and its core team includes Karina Vold, Christian Tarsney, and Gwen Bradford. Further details are available athttps://artificialconsciousness.ca/ACI, alongside the Department of Philosophy, invites applications for atwo-year postdoctoral fellowshipfocused on the philosophy of artificial intelligence, philosophy of mind, ethics, and/or decision theory. The expected start date is July 1, 2027, though the exact start-date of the contract is negotiable.Activities:The successful candidate will pursue an independent research program and contribute to the intellectual life of the Department of Philosophy and the Artificial Consciousness Initiative. The fellowship is a full-time research appointment, with up to 10% of hours allocated to administration and organization for ACI. The official academic unit is the Department of Philosophy, and the official supervisor is Andrew Y. Lee.Salary:The fellowship comes with a salary of at least CA$70,000 per annum, with additional salary possible from teaching (see below). The normal hours of work are 40 hours per week for a full-time postdoctoral fellow, recognizing that the needs of the employee's research and professional development and the needs of the supervisor's research program may require flexibility in the performance of the employee's duties and hours of work. (Should the minimum salary rates stipulated in the collective agreement become higher than the rates stated in this posting, the rate stated in this posting shall prevail.)Teaching: No teaching is required. However, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to apply for undergraduate Course Instructor positions in the Department of Philosophy, which are appointed and remunerated separately under the CUPE 3902 Unit 1 Collective Agreement. Any teaching would be remunerated separately at the standard Unit 1 rates (currently about CA$9,400–10,500 per half-course, plus vacation pay), without reducing the fellowship salary. We anticipate the ability to support the fellow in teaching one course (0.5 FCE) per year, subject to departmental need and the applicable appointment procedures.Further Details:All qualified applicants are invited to apply. The University of Toronto is strongly committed to diversity within its community and especially welcomesapplications from racialized persons / persons of colour, women, Indigenous / Aboriginal People of North America, persons with disabilities, LGBTQ2S+ persons, and others who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas. The University is committed to accessibility; applicants requiring accommodation at any stage of the application or hiring process should contact[email protected].Employment as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Toronto is covered by the terms of the CUPE 3902 Unit 5 Collective Agreement.Eligibility:To be eligible the successful candidate must have received a PhD in Philosophy (or a related field), and have fulfilled all conditions for conferral (including final approval of any post-defence corrections), before the starting date.Application:To ensure full consideration, applications should be submitted by 11:59pm (ET) onJanuary8,2027.Applicants should send the following documents (all in pdf format) to[email protected]:Cover Letter,CV,Research Statement,Writing Sample, with the title of the email in the form “LastName, FirstName ACI_Postdoc_2027.”Applicants should also solicitthreelettersof recommendation, sent to the same address, with the title of the email in the form “Letter: LastName, FirstName ACI_Postdoc_2027.”

jobs.description: The Department of Philosophy at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is the largest philosophy program in Hong Kong. It has consistently been ranked as the top Philosophy Department in Asia and one of the best worldwide. For more information about the department, please visit:http://www.phil.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/.PhD / Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Award(HKPFS) - (US$44,200 / year)The PhD fellowship is established by the Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong. The fellowship provides an annual stipend of approximately US$44,200 and a conference and research-related travel allowance of approximately US$1,850 per year for each awardee for a period of up to three years. Tuition fee during the student's normative study period will be waived.AdditionalScholarshipprovided by the CUHKHKPFS awardees will receive an additional scholarship provided by CUHK called the "CUHK Vice-Chancellor HKPFS Scholarship." This scholarship offers tuition waiver to HKPFS awardees for up to three years and an award of approximately US$5,130 for lodging in the first year of study and US$2,565 each in the second and third year. A conference and research-related travel allowance of approximately US$3,846 provided by the Graduate School and approximately US$1,538 provided by the Department are included. The scholarship also covers a tuition fee waiver for three years, and the on-campus hostel fee will be waived in the first year. Guaranteed on-campus accommodation is provided for the three years of study.Application ProcedureSubmit an initial application to the RGC through theironline application system (https://cerg1.ugc.edu.hk/hkpfs/InitApplication.jsp)and obtain a HKPFS reference number by 1 December 2026, 12:00 noon Hong Kong Time (or +8 hours GMT).Submit your full application throughCUHK’s Online Application System for Postgraduate Programmes (https://www.gs.cuhk.edu.hk/admissions/admissions/how-to-apply)and quote the HKPFS reference number by 1 December 2026, 11:59 pm Hong Kong Time (or +8 hours GMT).Applicants who arenominated to the HKPFS by CUHK but are not selectedfor the fellowship will be offered the CUHK Vice-Chancellor's PhD Scholarship. CUHK Vice-Chancellor's PhD Scholarship awardees receive an award of total approximately US$10,260 (1/2 in the first year of attendance and 1/4 each in the second and third years subject to satisfactory study progress).   An studentship of approximately US$29,400 per annum for three years will be provided.   Additionally, a conference and research-related travel allowance of approximately US$3,846 provided by the Graduate School and approximately US$1,538 provided by the Department are included.MPhil & PhD/Regular Postgraduate Studentships (US$29,400 / year)In addition to the more competitive Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme, the Philosophy Department of the Chinese University of Hong Kong also provides approximately 10 regular scholarships. These scholarships offer a studentship of approximately US$29,400 per annum for 3 years for PhD students and 2 years for Master of Philosophy students.Applicants for Hong Kong PhD fellowships who are not selected for these fellowships are automatically considered for our regular PhD scholarships. Applicants can also choose to apply solely for the regular PhD scholarships. For more information, please visithttps://phil.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/postgraduate/mphil-phd/admission/.

jobs.institution: Minnesota Center for Philosophy of Science, University of Minnesota
jobs.title: Post-Doctoral Associate
jobs.aos: Scholars working in all areas of philosophy of science, inclusive of philosophical approaches to logic and mathematics, are eligible. This is understood broadly to include general philosophy of science, as well as issues in the history and practice of particular sciences.
jobs.description: The Minnesota Center for Philosophy of Science (MCPS) in the College of Liberal Arts at the University of Minnesota invites applications for a full-time postdoctoral fellowship for a period of two years starting at the beginning the 2027 academic year (late August 2027).Applicants will have been awarded a doctorate in philosophy or history and philosophy of science within five years of the starting date of the position. Additionally, applicants must have had a dissertation project on or substantial publication in some topic in philosophy of science. Scholars working in all areas of philosophy of science, inclusive of philosophical approaches to logic and mathematics, are eligible. This is understood broadly to include general philosophy of science, as well as issues in the history and practice of particular sciences.Applications are encouraged from scholars with newly awarded doctorates in philosophy or history and philosophy of science at early stages of their career who have not yet secured a permanent academic position. Submissions from members of traditionally underrepresented groups are particularly welcome.The successful candidate will propose a focused project in philosophy of science to be undertaken and completed during the term of the position. The criteria for evaluation are the academic merit of the proposal and the academic strength of the candidate (demonstrated and potential research excellence and leadership), as well as the potential of the applicant to complement existing strengths of fellows and affiliates of the Minnesota Center for Philosophy of Science.The MCPS Postdoctoral Fellow is expected to reside in the Twin Cities metropolitan area, undertake research on a proposed project full-time in an office in the MCPS, and participate in the life of the MCPS by attending and contributing each academic term to at least one MCPS research group and participating in the joint weekly colloquium series with the History of Science, Technology, and Medicine Program, as well as special events (e.g., academic workshops). Additionally, in consultation with the Director of the MCPS, MCPS Postdoctoral Fellows will: (1) give an academic talk in the MCPS colloquium series on their research in their first semester in residence; (2) teach one undergraduate course on a topic in philosophy of science either in the third or fourth semester of their residence; and (3) co-lead an MCPS interest group in the third or fourth semester of their residence. MCPS Postdoctoral Fellows are not expected to undertake service responsibility for MCPS or the University of Minnesota. MCPS Postdoctoral Fellowships may not be deferred.The aim of this position is to support researchers within five years of their doctorate in alignment with and contributing toward the mission of the Minnesota Center for Philosophy of Science: to promote excellence in research and training in philosophy of science, related empirical studies of science, and science itself. This support is dedicated to a project in philosophy of science (broadly construed) that the applicant proposes.
jobs.instructions:

A curriculum vitae.

Letters of reference from three scholars knowledgeable of the applicant and the applicant’s work (sent separately to[email protected]; please use InterFolio where possible).


Documentation affirming that the requisite doctorate was or will be officially awarded, or that the applicant will have satisfied all formal requirements for the doctorate, including an unqualified acceptance of the dissertation manuscript and the unqualified passing of the oral exam, within the previous five years of the intended starting date of the fellowship.

jobs.institution: Center for Human Values and Program in Cognitive Science, Princeton University
jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in the Cognitive Science of Values
jobs.aos: cognitive science, psychology or empirically informed/experimental philosophy
jobs.description: The successful candidate will be based in the laboratory of Dr. Tania Lombrozo in the Department of Psychology. We aim to support a highly promising scholar with a background in cognitive science or a related discipline, such as psychology or empirically informed/experimental philosophy. The scholar's research agenda should address a topic that engages with both cognitive science and values, such as the role of moral values in decision making or the role of epistemic values in belief revision. The proposed research is expected to yield both theoretical and empirical publications. Candidates will be expected to contribute the equivalent of one course each year to the University Center and/or the Department. This contribution may be fulfilled by teaching a course on a topic related to cognitive science of values (subject to sufficient enrollments and approval by Project Directors, the Department Chair or Chairs, and the Office of the Dean of the Faculty) or service to the Project or Center of some other sort, subject to approval of the Project and Center Directors. If teaching a semester-long course, the successful candidate would carry the additional part-time rank of Lecturer. The postdoc will be expected to participate in a year-long research seminar for visiting fellows and Center faculty, as well as a year-long seminar for the Center’s cohort of Postdoctoral Associates. (Each of these seminars meets roughly every other week.)  The postdoc will also be expected to regularly attend talks, panels, and conferences sponsored by the Center.The candidate will be appointed in the Program in Cognitive Science and will be invited to participate in programs of the University Center for Human Values.

jobs.institution: University of Notre Dame Australia
jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Hebrew Philosophy
jobs.description:
About the projectThe University of Notre Dame Australia is proud to host the Arabic and Hebrew teams of the European Research Council (ERC) Synergy project, “Logic in Reverse Redux: Illegitimate Argumentative Moves in the Arabic, Byzantine, Hebrew and Latin Medieval Traditions,” (RevLogRedux), which is to run until 30 April 2031. The coordinating team of the Synergy Grant is led by Leone Gazziero at the CNRS, France; the Arabic team leader at UNDA is Tony Street and the Hebrew team leader is Charles Manekin. We seek to appoint up to twohighly research-active scholars working in medieval Hebrew philosophy with a track-record, or an interest in developing expertise, in researching medieval logical texts and fallacy-theory. In accordance with ERC conditions, all outcomes are to be published Open Access.About the roleThe Hebrew Traditionteam of the ERC project, “Logic in Reverse Redux: Illegitimate Argumentative Moves in the Arabic, Byzantine, Hebrew and Latin Medieval Traditions,” seeks to appoint up to two postdoctoral researchers. Participation in the project will be an opportunity to acquire new textual and philosophical skills, produce a significant research portfolio, develop ties with leading researchers in medieval philosophy, and be part of a major initiative in digital humanities. The team will engage actively with the other teams working on the Latin, Byzantine, Arabic rational and Arabic traditional sciences.As a guide, appointees will be expected to devote their time as follows: 20% transcribing, editing and translating a number of texts; 20% responding to the initiatives of the Geneva team as they develop AskSten; 60% conducting independent research on the historical and cultural context of the texts studied, and analysis of the fallacy-theories developed by Hebrew authors, especially as they relate to Aristotle’s Sophistical Refutations.These research-focused positions will contribute to the University's strategic research goals through the production of high-impact publications, including ERC-related outputs targeting leading Q1 journals or scholarly monographs. The role will strengthen the research profile of the Centre for the History of Philosophy, particularly in the growing field of Hebrew Philosophy, while supporting grant applications, research supervision and mentoring, and engaging in academic, professional, and research administration activities.
Key ResponsibilitiesContribute to the production of critical editions and translations of a corpus of medieval Hebrew texts on fallacies (seeherefor passages to be edited), preferably as the sole editor and translator for assigned passages, or, where necessary, as a team member working under the supervision of Professor Manekin.Undertake the transcription of texts not yet available in electronic format for inclusion in the project's web-based database.Conduct primary research on the historical and cultural context of the texts studied, and analysis of the fallacy-theories developed by Hebrew authors, especially as they relate to Aristotle’s Sophistical Refutations.Collaborate with the University of Geneva team in integrating materials from four philosophical traditions into AskSten, a multi-layered virtual research environment whose digital archive, knowledge base, Semantic Web architecture, and online deployment will enhance the formal expressiveness and coherence of the project's findings; seehttps://www.unige.ch/RevLog/about-1.Contribute to all activities associated with the ERC Synergy Grant, includingparticipating in conferences and workshops in the UK and Europe, help in organisingconferences and workshops, translation, independent research on topics related to the texts to be edited, and liaison with teams at CNRS, the University of Lille, and the University of Geneva to advance the project's objectives of collaboration and synergy.Post-docs are expected to participate in person in a fortnightly team seminar through the semester at the Broadway Campus.Qualifications, skills & experience
Essential:Research-level proficiency in the philosophical language of medieval Hebrew.Doctoral level training in Hebrew philosophy or medieval Jewish intellectual history, with evidence of potential for high-quality research; a strong publication record is highly desirable.Proficiency in Hebrew text entry, with the ability to read and interpret medieval manuscripts.Desirable:Background in digital humanities.Facility in another language in RevLog’s coverage (Latin, classical Greek, Arabic) or relevant to the study of the broader translation movement (Syriac).

jobs.institution: Global Commerce, Denison University
jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Global Commerce
jobs.aos: Research must focus on questions related to business, trade, or economic life
jobs.description: The Global Commerce program at Denison University invites applications for a tenure-track position at the assistant or associate professor level beginning in Fall 2027. Global Commerce takes an interdisciplinary approach to the study of business. The program trains students to think broadly and critically about how global exchanges of goods, services, information, and money shape and are shaped by a wide variety of economic, political, cultural, social, and environmental factors. Students in the program put this training into practice through consulting projects, entrepreneurial pitches, and a variety of co-curricular experiences. The current faculty includes scholars in history, economics, anthropology, organizational behavior, English, and philosophy.We are hiring a tenure-track faculty member from the humanities or humanistic social sciences whose research focuses on questions related to business, trade, or economic life. The hire will teach across our core curriculum, which includes an introductory course on the relationship between commerce and society, an introductory course on how businesses function in the modern economy, an intermediate course centering on a local business consulting project, and an advanced global entrepreneurship capstone in which students develop a business plan. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to develop commerce-related electives aligned with their research area.  (For more details on the Global Commerce curriculum, please see:https://denison.edu/academics/global-commerce.)The teaching load is 5 courses per year, the largest of which is capped at 25 students. A PhD is required by the time of appointment. Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to excellence in liberal arts teaching at the undergraduate level, a desire to contribute to the development of the Global Commerce major, and a willingness to work with our colleagues in the Knowlton Center for Career Exploration. Applicants must also demonstrate interest in integrating global perspectives into their teaching and working in an interdisciplinary program. We will consider the extent to which each candidate’s research perspective complements those currently represented in the Department. Applicants must also provide evidence of an active research agenda; continued scholarship is required of all tenure-track and tenured members of the Denison faculty. Additional work experience in the business, government, or non-profit sectors is strongly valued as a complement to academic expertise.Full consideration will be given to applications received byOctober 30th, 2026, though we will continue to accept applications until the position is filled. We expect candidates to have their PhD in hand by August 2027.Applicants should submit the following electronic application materials on-line: (1) a cover letter that explains the candidate’s commitment to liberal arts teaching and discusses the candidate’s interest in our interdisciplinary, practically-oriented approach to the study of Global Commerce; (2) a curriculum vitae; (3) a teaching statement or portfolio that lays out the candidate's teaching philosophy, interests, and experience; (4) a 1-2 page description of the candidate’s research agenda; (5) a writing sample; and (6) a list of three academic references (upon narrowing our pool of candidates, we will ask for letters).

Given our location in Silicon Valley and our commitment to supporting the development of ethical technologies through our newAdvanced Institute for Ethical Technologies, there are significant interdisciplinary collaborative opportunities for a faculty member exploring these issues through a philosophical lens. The Institute, in the process of being formed, pursues the need for human-centered technology that values privacy and ethical decision-making.  In partnership with the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Library and the San Jose Public Library, the College has also established theDigital Humanities Centeras a site of curriculum development, faculty research, student engagement, and public-facing programming and events.The Department of Philosophy (https://www.sjsu.edu/philosophy/) is one of ten departments and schools in the College of Humanities & the Arts (https://www.sjsu.edu/humanitiesandarts/departments.php) and offers Philosophy BA and MA programs. We value and engage with a plurality of philosophical traditions and styles, as well as the perspectives of our diverse community of faculty and students. We are committed to creating learning environments, a departmental culture, and a larger philosophical community that welcomes all who want to explore philosophy.The Department of Philosophy and San José State University value institutional excellence and are committed to advancing equity through research, teaching, and service. We enroll more than 40,000 students, many of whom are historically underserved; approximately 45% of our undergraduate students are first-generation college students and 38% are Pell Grant recipients. In addition, we are both a Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander Serving Institution (AANAPISI). SJSU aspires to create holistic learning environments that facilitate both individual and collective transformation. We seek teacher-scholars who cultivate inclusive, empowering spaces for mutual learning, skill-building, and knowledge exchange for all students. Our commitment to lifelong learning supports meaningful connections among faculty, staff, students, alumni, and the broader communities we serve.We invite all applicants to include a Statement of Institutional Excellence (or incorporate it into your cover letter) to share how your lived and professional experiences will contribute to the SJSU community—particularly in relation to student success. jobs.description: Position DescriptionJohns Hopkins University’sSchool of Government and Policyseeks to recruit multiple tenured and tenure-track faculty in multiple disciplines and fields of study, including (but not limited to) political science, law, sociology, history, philosophy, computer science, and economics.While searching broadly, we have a particular interest in faculty conducting research on the following topics of inquiry:Cities and Communities:State and local policymaking and implementation. Applications are encouraged from candidates in civil engineering, economics, history, law, sociology, political science, public administration, or urban planning, with research interests including local governance, state capacity, urban innovation, housing and real estate, public education and school choice, transportation and land use, or local finance and budgeting.Frontier AI:The implications of highly advanced AI for government and society. Applications are encouraged from candidates from a wide range of disciplines including computer science, economics, philosophy, law, political science cognitive science, and sociology. Research interests might include: AI alignment and governance; the government, societal, and labor market impacts of and adaptation to AI; the use of AI to simulate and design policy interventions; regulatory theory and innovation; institutional design and innovation; and AI evaluation, auditing and verification.Political Philosophy and Theory:Ambitious, foundational, big-picture political philosophy and/or political theory with direct relevance to government and policy, advancing the school's mission of shoring up and renewing the core institutions of liberal democracy. Applications are encouraged from candidates who are problem-focused and syncretistic, drawing on different conceptual, methodological, and empirical approaches and orienting themselves outward from philosophy/theory toward the world, with particular interest in candidates whose work intersects with or complements other parts of the School's research strengths.Public-Sector Innovation and Management:How governments and other public-sector organizations function, why they succeed or fail, and how to change them to more effectively solve public problems. Applications are encouraged from candidates in the social sciences, management, history, organizational behavior, psychology, urban planning, operations research, industrial and systems engineering, management science, public management, or public policy. Research interests might include: institutional reform and organizational change; public innovation and problem solving; public-sector management, budgeting, procurement, contracting, and operations; state capacity and bureaucratic performance; organizational structure, behavior, learning, and culture; the adoption and management of technology in government, including the organizational challenges of effective implementation and how technologies affect public-sector organizations, policy, and governance.Regulation, Bureaucracy, and Public Administration:Why governments so often fail to deliver what policies promise, and what institutional redesigns would enable them to do so. Applications are encouraged from candidates in political science, law, public administration, history, sociology, or other fields whose work is changing the terms of academic and public debate. Research interests might include: the politics of civil service and personnel systems; federalism and the implementation of large public programs; intergovernmental relations; regulation, enforcement, and capture; administrative procedure and policy analysis; or state capacity more broadly.Across all these searches, we seek candidates who can work and learn across disciplines and take seriously the need to improve government effectiveness. We welcome candidates who have worked within public-sector and policymaking institutions and alongside government reformers from across the political spectrum. We are also interested in candidates who wish to investigate the challenges and opportunities of governing and deploying artificial intelligence.About the School of Government and PolicyAnchored at the Hopkins Bloomberg Center in the heart of Washington, D.C., the School of Government and Policy will be a hub of discovery, collaboration, and impact. At a time of political, social, and technological upheaval, this new school will support and inform scholarly and practical efforts to build a more effective government and solve complex policy challenges. The school will scrutinize institutional reforms that have the potential to improve government operations, examine the potential for advancing technologies to transform government workforces and operations, develop novel approaches to multidisciplinary education and experiential learning, and foster vital dialogue and engagement across a wide range of worldviews, backgrounds, and epistemologies.Similar to JHU’s other academic divisions, the School of Government and Policy will be grounded in a commitment to both world-class research and exceptional education. It will prepare the next generation of policy and public sector leaders to advance evidence-based solutions to society’s greatest challenges through innovative approaches that: 1) embed science, data, and technology in curricula; 2) give students the tools required to think strategically and creatively about government and policy innovations; and 3) emphasize the critical need for cross-functional skills and capabilities at all levels of government and in bridging public, non-profit, and industry sectors.We are building a community of scholars, experts, and leaders from a wide range of disciplines who embrace intellectual pluralism—with the intention not merely of representing different perspectives and ways of understanding, but of putting these differences to good use. We welcome applications from scholars who challenge conventional thinking through rigorous inquiry.Over the course of its founding years, the school will grow to encompass 35 full-time faculty members with expertise that spans both theoretical and applied approaches to public policy and government. During this founding period, additional hires will be made with other units across the University, yielding an even larger and more integrated tenured and tenure-track faculty.Assistant Professor:QualificationsApplicants must hold a Ph.D. in an appropriate field or J.D. by the time their appointment begins. Candidates must have demonstrated an ability to conduct outstanding independent research and show promise for excellent teaching, mentoring, and public engagement.Application InstructionsInterested applicants should submit a cover letter, CV, two writing samples, and three letters of recommendation. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis and should be received by October 25, 2026 for full consideration. Interested candidates should submit their applications via Interfolio.Dependent upon discipline, rank, and other factors listed below, the overall expected salary range for this position is $100,000 to $200,000.Associate / Full Professor:QualificationsApplicants must hold a Ph.D. in an appropriate field or J.D. by the time their appointment begins. Candidates must have a demonstrated ability to conduct outstanding independent research and a strong record of excellence in teaching, mentoring, and public engagement.Application InstructionsInterested applicants should submit a cover letter and CV. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis and should be received by October 25, 2026 for full consideration. Interested candidates should submit their applications via Interfolio.Dependent upon discipline, rank, and other factors listed below, the overall expected salary range for these positions is $175,000 to $425,000.

jobs.description: Department of PhilosophyTenure-Track Assistant Professor in Political PhilosophyThe Department of Philosophy at the College of the Holy Cross invites applications for a full-time tenure-track Assistant Professor specializing in Political Philosophy to begin in August 2027. The ideal candidate will have an Area of Specialization in Political Philosophy with an emphasis on the foundations of democracy. Within this AOS, we plan to look for Areas of Concentration in deliberative democracy, epistemological aspects of democracy, philosophy of law, pluralism, and non-state democracy. We expect such a candidate to meet needs at both the departmental and institutional level by teaching courses in the above-mentioned areas and perhaps by participating in interdisciplinary courses and related activities and programs offered by the College. Successful candidates will demonstrate excellence as both teachers and scholars. As teachers, we seek candidates with a demonstrated commitment toinnovative, inclusive excellence in teaching.  As scholars, we seek candidates with an active, fruitful research agenda who are cognizant of our obligations to the wider community.This position carries a 3-2 teaching load with a research leave prior to tenure review of either a full year at 80% salary or a semester at full salary, and generous sabbatical and fellowship leaves for tenured faculty. To enable a smooth transition to Holy Cross, new full-time tenure-track Assistant Professors receive start-up funding to support their research and professional development and have a one-course reduction in their first year of teaching (i.e., 2-2). This position offers full benefits and a starting salary of $102,500.In alignment with the strategic plans forHoly Crossandthe division of Academic Affairs, we view academic excellence and inclusive excellence as inextricably linked. Our faculty combine high-impact scholarship and outstanding teaching with a deep commitment to inclusive excellence. They generate new knowledge in their fields while utilizing evidence-based teaching strategies and course designs to create classroom environments where all students have a sense of belonging, are valued, and can flourish to reach their full potential. Academic freedom is a cornerstone of our intellectual and moral community; the College is committed to supporting faculty and students as they work to advance our educational mission and serve the common good.QUALIFICATIONSCandidates must demonstrate excellence in scholarship and undergraduate teaching as well as a commitment to inclusive pedagogies. A Ph.D. in Philosophy is required by the beginning of the appointment.APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONSPlease submit1. A cover letter addressing the position requirements listed above as well as the ways you might contribute to and further theCollege’s missionas a Jesuit, undergraduate liberal arts college and its core commitmentto creating a communitywhere every individual feels empowered to contribute their talents and perspectives. 2. A curriculum vitae.  3. Unofficial undergraduate and graduate transcripts. 4. A statement of your teaching philosophy and interests, with particular emphasis on how you utilize evidence-based teaching strategies to foster inclusive, high-belonging classroom environments. 5. 3 Confidential Letters of Recommendation 6. A Writing Sample (preferably published, but can be ‘in process’ as well) 7. A Research statement that communicates the candidate's current scholarly focus and future trajectoryThe College of the Holy Cross uses Interfolio to collect all faculty job applications. Please submit all materials tohttps://apply.interfolio.com/193949.For full consideration, please apply by November 1. Initial interviews via Zoom will take place in December 5-8, and campus visits for finalists will take place in February 9-18. Questions about this search may be directed to Professor Jeffrey Bernstein,[email protected].The Provost’s Office supportsthe Association of American Universities’ principleson preventing sexual harassment in academia. Accordingly, all finalists will be asked to attest that they are not currently under investigation for sexual misconduct and that there are no substantiated findings of sexual misconduct against them in any previous position—or, if such findings exist, to provide a full explanation. The candidate selected for an offer will also be asked to provide written consent for the release of personnel information from their prior employer.For applicants who may require visa sponsorship: The College supports new faculty in pursuing an appropriate visa or other immigration status consistent with their qualifications and the responsibilities of the position. Because several pathways may be available, the College works with candidates who are offered positions to determine the most appropriate option. jobs.description: Position Title: Endowed Bartlett Chair Professor/Associate Professor, Free SpeechReq ID: R0006507Time Type: Full timeLocation: Waltham, MADescription:Job Description SummaryBentley University invites applications for the Bartlett Chair of Free Speech, an endowed position at the Associate or Full Professor level, to begin in Fall 2027.Funded by a generous gift from Bruce and Patricia Bartlett, this professorship affirms Bentley's commitment to fostering free expression, intellectual pluralism, and the constructive exchange of ideas as central to a liberal education.This position is part of a broader Bartlett Initiative that also includes a companion Chair of Free Enterprise. environments in which students can engage constructively with competing ideas and perspectives.Scholarship and External EngagementMaintain an active and visible research agenda related to free speech, free expression, or closely connected areas of inquiry.Publish in scholarly journals and public-facing venues.Present research and ideas at national and international conferences, public forums, and professional gatherings.Contribute to public conversations about free expression, academic freedom, and civil discourse through writing, speaking, media engagement, or related activities.Develop and sustain relationships with relevant scholarly, professional, and civic organizations, which may include the Academic Freedom Alliance, Heterodox Academy, the Foundation for Individual Rights and jobs.description: About the roleThe full-time postdoctoral fellow in philosophy will conduct independent and collaborative research in the Philosophical Moral Psychology Lab under the supervision of Dr Joanna Demaree-Cotton. The post is fixed term for 3 years. The fellow will work as part of a collaborative interdisciplinary team contributing to projects within the Philosophical Moral Psychology Lab. Though they may work on various topics in the lab, the fellow’s research will include contributions to the Moral Psychology of Autonomy in Healthcare project, looking at topics such as: autonomy-based rights in healthcare; inequities in respect for medical autonomy; what it means to be ‘listened to’; whether there are moral duties of listening; cross-cultural understandings of medical autonomy and patient consent.   The lab includes researchers with complementary skills in philosophical and psychological methods respectively. The fellow will be expected to collaborate with researchers whose expertise lies in experimental moral psychology.   The fellow will be expected to actively contribute to research relevant to the Philosophical Moral Psychology Lab, and also provide guidance to junior members of the research group including research assistants, PhD students, and/or project volunteers.  The Philosophical Moral Psychology Lab conducts interdisciplinary research that draws on moral philosophy, ethics, experimental philosophy and moral psychology. The lab investigates the factors and psychological processes that shape moral intuitions, moral reasoning, and moral agency, and develops empirically-informed contributions to normative debates in philosophical ethics. Current research areas include: consent and autonomy; gender bias and medical ethics; moral dilemmas; moral responsibility and blame; moral duties to the dead; animal and AI ethics. For more information about the research group, see https://moralpsychlab.web.ox.ac.uk/home.   The start date of the role is 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter, and no later than 1 October 2027.About youYou will hold a PhD or DPhil in Philosophy (or related field), or be close to completion by the advertised closing date for this application.   It is essential for the postholder to have expertise in ethics and moral philosophy. The possession of interdisciplinary skills is desirable, and interest in relevant interdisciplinary research (e.g. psychologically-informed ethics, philosophically-informed moral psychology, experimental philosophy, and/or philosophy of psychology) is essential. The successful candidate will have demonstrated excellent research skills and willingness to work collaboratively with others.   The duties and skills required are described in further detail in the job description, which can be found at the above link.

jobs.description: Stetson University seeks a broadly trained teacher-scholar with an area of competence in the philosophy of law or a related philosophical area with legal experience relevant to the position.This is a full-time, 9-month position beginning in August 2027.QUALIFICATIONS:A Ph.D. in Philosophy, or in a closely related field with substantial graduate preparation in philosophy, completed by August 2027. The successful candidate will have an active scholarly agenda and demonstrated excellence in teaching undergraduates. The University seeks a broadly trained teacher-scholar with an area of competence in the philosophy of law or a related philosophical area with legal experience relevant to the position. With respect to legal experience, a J.D. is preferred. However, candidates with comparable legal preparation or substantial professional experience in legal practice, courts, government, public-interest advocacy, mediation, regulatory or compliance work, or legal education will also receive full consideration. Experience with pre-law advising, LSAT preparation, or coaching Mock Trial or Moot Court is welcome but not required. The ability to teach Introduction to Logic is also desirable.RESPONSIBILITIES:The annual teaching load includes five regular courses and one student-centered immersive experience (equivalent to one course) as a part of the University’s experiential, contemporary, and integrative learning initiative – Hatter Ready. Teaching responsibilities will include introductory and advanced courses in the candidate’s areas of competence, regular contributions to law-related undergraduate programming, and courses in Stetson’s General Education curriculum. Depending on the candidate’s expertise, courses might include Philosophy of Law, Political Philosophy, constitutionalism, theories of rights and justice, legal reasoning and interpretation, or other philosophically informed courses concerning law and legal institutions. The successful candidate will also help strengthen connections among the Philosophy Department, the Law Ready curriculum, Stetson’s broader pre-law programming, and Stetson’s College of Law.For more information on our expectations in teaching and scholarship, our tenure policies, and our support for faculty development, please see the Academic Affairs website at https://www.stetson.edu/administration/provost/prospective-faculty/index.php.The successful candidate will contribute to Stetson’s growing Law Ready undergraduate curriculum, which serves approximately 300 students interested in attending law school. Law Ready brings together interdisciplinary coursework, the Law, Society, and Advocacy and Business Law minors, a living-learning community, pre-law advising, and experiential opportunities such as Mock Trial and Moot Court. Stetson’s Mock Trial team is currently ranked number one in Florida, providing students with an exceptional opportunity to develop practical skills in trial advocacy alongside the excellence of Stetson Law’s trial-advocacy programs.Law Ready approaches preparation for law school through the liberal arts. We therefore seek a colleague who can help students develop the close reading, analytical reasoning, clear writing, oral advocacy, ethical reflection, and understanding of legal institutions needed for success in law school and civic life. The successful candidate should be prepared to engage students seriously and respectfully with competing positions on contested legal, moral, and political questions.THE DEPARTMENT:Stetson’s Department of Philosophy takes a rigorous, interdisciplinary, and pluralistic approach to undergraduate liberal arts education. The successful candidate will join a close-knit department as its third full-time faculty member. Our faculty are active scholars with strong publication records and wide-ranging interests in analytic, continental, feminist, historical, experimental, and applied philosophy. We work deliberately to create a welcoming intellectual home for philosophy students through close mentoring, undergraduate research, and immersive activities such as Philosophy Club, Idle Talk, and a Film Club. The department is also closely connected to Stetson’s expanding pre-law initiatives: its chair currently serves as Pre-Law Director for the University’s Law Ready program.THE COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES:Stetson’s College of Arts and Sciences (https://www.stetson.edu/artsci/) is the largest and most diverse of the University’s colleges and schools; it includes the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, education, and creative arts. With nineteen academic departments and nine interdisciplinary programs, the College is the liberal arts core of the University. A great strength of the College is its faculty of approximately 140 full-time teacher-scholars. The College offers 31 undergraduate majors and 34 undergraduate minors; seven graduate degrees are offered in Education, Counselor Education, and Creative Writing. Every undergraduate major requires a senior research project, allowing students the opportunity to design and carry out independent research under faculty mentorship. Our academic programs are shaped by the values of social justice and civic responsibility. All of our courses and programs of study promote engaged learning, whereby students create connections between the classroom or lab and the local, regional, and global community. The academic programs of the College of Arts and Sciences prepare students to live significant lives, to interact with and positively affect the world around them.THE UNIVERSITY:Founded in 1883, Stetson University (http://www.stetson.edu) is a private, selective university comprised of a rich array of liberal arts and professional academic programs. Collectively, Stetson’s faculty works with approximately 3,700 students in undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs. The University’s historic main campus, located in DeLand, enrolls approximately 2,300 students in undergraduate programs in the College of Arts and Sciences, the School of Business Administration, and the School of Music. Stetson University College of Law, Florida’s first law school, moved from the main campus to Gulfport in 1954, and, with the addition of the Tampa Law Center, serves approximately 1,000 students working full-time or part-time toward J.D. or LL.M. degrees. Graduate programs based at the main campus in DeLand include Business, Accounting, Education, Counseling, and Creative Writing, with Educational Leadership cohorts also offered at the Gulfport campus. Stetson is Florida’s oldest private institution of higher learning and was the first private college in Florida to be granted a chapter of Phi Beta Kappa.Stetson University provides an inspiring education that engages students with rigorous academic and creative study grounded in liberal learning and promotes civic values of personal and social responsibility. Working closely with faculty and with one another, students cultivate abilities to explore issues deeply, think critically, reason empirically, speak persuasively, and connect ideas creatively. Firmly committed to inclusive excellence, our vibrant community of teacher-scholars nurtures the potential of individual students to lead lives of significance and prepares each to meet the challenges of shaping the future—locally, nationally, and globally.THE COMMUNITY:DeLand is a picturesque residential community of 38,000 located 20 miles west of Daytona Beach and 35 miles northeast of Orlando. The area offers extensive cultural as well as recreational activities.SALARY:Salary is competitive.STARTING DATE: August 9, 2027.APPLICATION:Applicants are asked to supply:a cover letter that includes a statement about the candidate’s teaching and research interests, experience relevant to the position, and a discussion of how the candidate proposes to develop as a teacher-scholara teaching portfolio, inclusive of teaching philosophy, sample syllabi (classes taught or that you would like to teach), and student evaluations for courses taught (where available)a curriculum vitaethe names, addresses, e-mail addresses, and telephone numbers of three professional references to be contacted later in the processIn the cover letter, candidates are encouraged to highlight skills and experiences that demonstrate a commitment to promoting inclusive academic environments and engaging across differences.Please visit our Career Opportunities Website (https://www.schooljobs.com/careers/stetson/delandfaculty?) to apply and to upload your application documents.Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.WORK AUTHORIZATION REQUIREMENTS:Work authorization sponsorship may be available for this position. However, sponsorship is contingent upon the non-applicability of the visa petition fees outlined in the relevant Executive Order. International candidates are encouraged to apply, but should be aware that eligibility for sponsorship will be evaluated in accordance with current U.S. immigration regulations and institutional policies.Stetson University is an Equal Opportunity Employer that affirms inclusive environments and engaging across differences as a core value of academic excellence in which all employees and candidates are treated equally no matter their age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, military status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, or shared ancestry. We are committed to achieving equal access in education, employment, and participation through the recruitment and retention of outstanding faculty, staff, and students from a tapestry of backgrounds, and to meaningful academic and intellectual transformation in curriculum, research and service.We are dedicated to actions and policies that foster a community in which individuals across all identities, cultures, backgrounds, and viewpoints work together to create opportunities for engagement through rewarding and fulfilling careers and personal experiences in an increasingly diverse society and a globalized world. We encourage qualified candidates across all backgrounds and identities to apply for employment.  Stetson University is an EEO, ADA, ADEA, and GINA employer.

Responsibilities include undergraduate and graduate (master’s level) teaching at the standard load (2/2 for research-active faculty), research, advising, and committee work. Ph.D. required by the start date.Northern Illinois University (NIU) is one of the largest public universities in the state of Illinois, with approximately 16,000 students. NIU is a Carnegie Doctoral/Research University-Higher Research Activity institution located in DeKalb, an affordable and growing community 65 miles west of Chicago. We strive to improve outcomes for all students by identifying and removing barriers that disproportionately hinder the academic achievement and student experience of historically and currently underserved populations. The Department of Philosophy is committed to building and sustaining inclusive and equitable working and learning environments for all its students, staff, and faculty. It offers both a baccalaureate program and a terminal master’s program.Position SummaryThe Assistant Professor of Philosophy will be an active researcher who teaches undergraduate and graduate courses for the Department of Philosophy. new_jobs.description: The Department of Philosophy in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Kentucky invites applications for a tenure-eligible position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor specializing in ethics. This is a nine-month appointment in the regular title series with an anticipated start date of August 1, 2027. The anticipated Distribution of Effort will be 45% teaching, 45% research, and 10% departmental service.The successful candidate will demonstrate a well-developed research program with strong potential for continued scholarly productivity and evidence of effective teaching. The position carries a teaching load of two courses per semester, including courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels. The successful candidate will also contribute to graduate advising and participate in departmental and university service.The Department is particularly interested in candidates whose research or teaching complements a primary specialization in ethics with interests in applied ethics and/or the ethics of artificial intelligence. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the development of a course in AI ethics.The University of Kentucky Department of Philosophy is a pluralistic department that welcomes diverse approaches to philosophical research and teaching. A PhD in Philosophy or a related field is required at time of appointment.

new_jobs.description: The Department of Philosophy at the University of Illinois Chicago invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position beginning August 16, 2027. We are looking for applicants whose work focuses on philosophical issues raised by AI or related technologies. The successful applicant will be expected to develop and regularly teach undergraduate courses on the philosophy of computing and the ethics of computing and AI that serve as core courses for the Computer Science + Philosophy program. In addition, we are looking for someone capable of building interdisciplinary connections between the philosophy department and those departments concerned with computational science. The teaching load is two courses per semester, and faculty are expected to be research active and to provide service to the department and university. UIC faculty are expected to carry out their responsibilities in person and onsite as part of a vibrant and collegial on-campus community.Minimum qualifications: PhD expected prior to start date, evidence of teaching effectiveness and research accomplishment in the area of focus.The budgeted salary range for this position is$100,000-$120,000with an anticipated startup fund of $30,000 ($10,000 a year for 3 years). Final authorization of the position is subject to availability of funding.This position is intended to beeligible for benefits. This includes Health, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, a Retirement Plan, Paid time Off, and Tuition waivers for employees and dependents.For fullest consideration, please complete the on-line application with the names and email addresses of at least three references and upload a cover letter, CV, writing sample, research statement, and teaching portfolio that speaks to how you would teach the two courses mentioned above byOctober 21, 2026The closing date for the posting is December 2, 2026.The University of Illinois Chicago is a Carnegie Doctoral/Research-Extensive University located in the heart of one of the nation's largest metropolitan areas. It is a comprehensive public university with a diverse student body of more than 30,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students. UIC is federally recognized as a Minority Serving Institution (MSI) through its status as an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander Serving Institution (AANAPISI) and a Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI), fully funded by the U.S. Department of Education.The University of Illinois System is an equal opportunity employer, including but not limited to disability and/or veteran status, and complies with all applicable state and federal employment mandates. new_jobs.description: The University of Toronto Artificial Consciousness Initiative (ACI) is a three-year pilot project advancing foundational research connecting artificial intelligence and consciousness. The project is led by Andrew Y. Lee, and its core team includes Karina Vold, Christian Tarsney, and Gwen Bradford. Further details are available athttps://artificialconsciousness.ca/ACI, alongside the Department of Philosophy, invites applications for atwo-year postdoctoral fellowshipfocused on the philosophy of artificial intelligence, philosophy of mind, ethics, and/or decision theory. The expected start date is July 1, 2027, though the exact start-date of the contract is negotiable.Activities:The successful candidate will pursue an independent research program and contribute to the intellectual life of the Department of Philosophy and the Artificial Consciousness Initiative. The fellowship is a full-time research appointment, with up to 10% of hours allocated to administration and organization for ACI. The official academic unit is the Department of Philosophy, and the official supervisor is Andrew Y. Lee.Salary:The fellowship comes with a salary of at least CA$70,000 per annum, with additional salary possible from teaching (see below). The normal hours of work are 40 hours per week for a full-time postdoctoral fellow, recognizing that the needs of the employee's research and professional development and the needs of the supervisor's research program may require flexibility in the performance of the employee's duties and hours of work. (Should the minimum salary rates stipulated in the collective agreement become higher than the rates stated in this posting, the rate stated in this posting shall prevail.)Teaching: No teaching is required. However, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to apply for undergraduate Course Instructor positions in the Department of Philosophy, which are appointed and remunerated separately under the CUPE 3902 Unit 1 Collective Agreement. Any teaching would be remunerated separately at the standard Unit 1 rates (currently about CA$9,400–10,500 per half-course, plus vacation pay), without reducing the fellowship salary. We anticipate the ability to support the fellow in teaching one course (0.5 FCE) per year, subject to departmental need and the applicable appointment procedures.Further Details:All qualified applicants are invited to apply. The University of Toronto is strongly committed to diversity within its community and especially welcomesapplications from racialized persons / persons of colour, women, Indigenous / Aboriginal People of North America, persons with disabilities, LGBTQ2S+ persons, and others who may contribute to the further diversification of ideas. The University is committed to accessibility; applicants requiring accommodation at any stage of the application or hiring process should contact[email protected].Employment as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Toronto is covered by the terms of the CUPE 3902 Unit 5 Collective Agreement.Eligibility:To be eligible the successful candidate must have received a PhD in Philosophy (or a related field), and have fulfilled all conditions for conferral (including final approval of any post-defence corrections), before the starting date.Application:To ensure full consideration, applications should be submitted by 11:59pm (ET) onJanuary8,2027.Applicants should send the following documents (all in pdf format) to[email protected]:Cover Letter,CV,Research Statement,Writing Sample, with the title of the email in the form “LastName, FirstName ACI_Postdoc_2027.”Applicants should also solicitthreelettersof recommendation, sent to the same address, with the title of the email in the form “Letter: LastName, FirstName ACI_Postdoc_2027.”

new_jobs.description: The Philosophy Discipline in the Department of Language, Culture, and the Arts, College of Arts, Sciences, and Letters (CASL) at the University of Michigan-Dearborn invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Philosophy, with an area of specialization in Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence and an area of competence in Philosophy of Science or Philosophy of Mind. The preferred starting date is September 2027.Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in Philosophy by the time of appointment and demonstrate strong potential for excellence in research and teaching.The Philosophy Discipline is committed to excellence in undergraduate education and scholarship. Philosophy serves students from across the university through high-enrollment foundational courses as well as upper-level courses in a broad range of philosophical areas. The successful candidate will contribute to the continued development of the Philosophy curriculum, particularly in Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence and related areas, and will have opportunities for interdisciplinary engagement with programs and faculty across the university.Teaching responsibilities are based on a 2–2 teaching load and will include courses in the candidate’s areas of specialization and competence, as well as foundational Philosophy courses such as Introduction to Philosophy, Critical Thinking, and Ethics. The successful candidate will be expected to develop and teach courses in Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence and related areas, which may include AI Ethics and Philosophy of Technology.The successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active program of scholarly research appropriate to a tenure-track appointment and to contribute service to the Philosophy Discipline, the Department of Language, Culture, and the Arts, the College, the University, and the profession.This is an on-site position, and the successful candidate will be expected to teach in a variety of modalities, including in-person, hybrid, and online courses.Required qualifications:Ph.D. in Philosophy completed by the time of appointment.Area of specialization in Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence.Area of competence in Philosophy of Science or Philosophy of Mind.Evidence of, or strong potential for, excellence in philosophical research.Evidence of, or strong potential for, excellence in undergraduate teaching.Ability to teach foundational undergraduate Philosophy courses, including courses such as Introduction to Philosophy, Critical Thinking, and Ethics.Ability to develop and teach courses in Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence and related areas.Preferred qualificationsDemonstrated potential for interdisciplinary teaching, research, or collaboration involving artificial intelligence and related areas.Experience with, or interest in, developing connections between Philosophy and other academic disciplines or programs.Campus and Community InformationThe University of Michigan-Dearborn was founded in 1959 on 200 acres of the original Henry Ford Estate in Dearborn, Michigan. As one of the three campuses of the University of Michigan, we serve over 8,000 students and provide high-quality undergraduate, graduate, professional, and continuing education programs that embody the prestige of the University of Michigan name. Our mission is rooted in commitment to the well-being and diversity of Metro Detroit, fostering a caring, dynamic, intellectual, and socially welcoming environment.We distinguish ourselves by building and nurturing intentional, mutually beneficial partnerships with local industries, governments, and community organizations. Our faculty are recognized for their excellence in scholarship and teaching and are actively engaged in professional and academic service. UM-Dearborn offers ample opportunities for creative, collaborative research, practice-based learning, and community engagement through scholarly and educational partnerships.Faculty have the privilege to work closely with their students, 47% of whom are first-generation college students, 46% Pell Grant eligible, and 31% students of color. The average class size is 25 students, and 69% of classes have fewer than 30 students. U.S. News & World Report consistently ranks UM-Dearborn among the best regional universities in the Midwest. In 2024, UM-Dearborn was ranked the number one regional public university in Michigan and third in the Midwest. The university is also recognized on Forbes' list of America's Top Colleges.Dearborn is a vibrant and diverse community, centrally located within one of America's largest business regions. The area provides a variety of urban, suburban, and rural environments within a reasonable commute, including Detroit, its suburbs, and Ann Arbor.Background ScreeningThe University of Michigan conducts background checks on all job candidates upon acceptance of a contingent offer and may use a third-party administrator to conduct background checks. Background checks will be performed in compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act.U-M EEO StatementThe University of Michigan is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

Submissions from members of traditionally underrepresented groups are particularly welcome.The successful candidate will propose a focused project in philosophy of science to be undertaken and completed during the term of the position. Additionally, in consultation with the Director of the MCPS, MCPS Postdoctoral Fellows will: (1) give an academic talk in the MCPS colloquium series on their research in their first semester in residence; (2) teach one undergraduate course on a topic in philosophy of science either in the third or fourth semester of their residence; and (3) co-lead an MCPS interest group in the third or fourth semester of their residence. new_jobs.title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Hebrew Philosophy
new_jobs.description:
About the projectThe University of Notre Dame Australia is proud to host the Arabic and Hebrew teams of the European Research Council (ERC) Synergy project, “Logic in Reverse Redux: Illegitimate Argumentative Moves in the Arabic, Byzantine, Hebrew and Latin Medieval Traditions,” (RevLogRedux), which is to run until 30 April 2031. The coordinating team of the Synergy Grant is led by Leone Gazziero at the CNRS, France; the Arabic team leader at UNDA is Tony Street and the Hebrew team leader is Charles Manekin. We seek to appoint up to twohighly research-active scholars working in medieval Hebrew philosophy with a track-record, or an interest in developing expertise, in researching medieval logical texts and fallacy-theory. In accordance with ERC conditions, all outcomes are to be published Open Access.About the roleThe Hebrew Traditionteam of the ERC project, “Logic in Reverse Redux: Illegitimate Argumentative Moves in the Arabic, Byzantine, Hebrew and Latin Medieval Traditions,” seeks to appoint up to two postdoctoral researchers. Participation in the project will be an opportunity to acquire new textual and philosophical skills, produce a significant research portfolio, develop ties with leading researchers in medieval philosophy, and be part of a major initiative in digital humanities. The team will engage actively with the other teams working on the Latin, Byzantine, Arabic rational and Arabic traditional sciences.As a guide, appointees will be expected to devote their time as follows: 20% transcribing, editing and translating a number of texts; 20% responding to the initiatives of the Geneva team as they develop AskSten; 60% conducting independent research on the historical and cultural context of the texts studied, and analysis of the fallacy-theories developed by Hebrew authors, especially as they relate to Aristotle’s Sophistical Refutations.These research-focused positions will contribute to the University's strategic research goals through the production of high-impact publications, including ERC-related outputs targeting leading Q1 journals or scholarly monographs. The role will strengthen the research profile of the Centre for the History of Philosophy, particularly in the growing field of Hebrew Philosophy, while supporting grant applications, research supervision and mentoring, and engaging in academic, professional, and research administration activities.
Key ResponsibilitiesContribute to the production of critical editions and translations of a corpus of medieval Hebrew texts on fallacies (seeherefor passages to be edited), preferably as the sole editor and translator for assigned passages, or, where necessary, as a team member working under the supervision of Professor Manekin.Undertake the transcription of texts not yet available in electronic format for inclusion in the project's web-based database.Conduct primary research on the historical and cultural context of the texts studied, and analysis of the fallacy-theories developed by Hebrew authors, especially as they relate to Aristotle’s Sophistical Refutations.Collaborate with the University of Geneva team in integrating materials from four philosophical traditions into AskSten, a multi-layered virtual research environment whose digital archive, knowledge base, Semantic Web architecture, and online deployment will enhance the formal expressiveness and coherence of the project's findings; seehttps://www.unige.ch/RevLog/about-1.Contribute to all activities associated with the ERC Synergy Grant, includingparticipating in conferences and workshops in the UK and Europe, help in organisingconferences and workshops, translation, independent research on topics related to the texts to be edited, and liaison with teams at CNRS, the University of Lille, and the University of Geneva to advance the project's objectives of collaboration and synergy.Post-docs are expected to participate in person in a fortnightly team seminar through the semester at the Broadway Campus.Qualifications, skills & experience
Essential:Research-level proficiency in the philosophical language of medieval Hebrew.Doctoral level training in Hebrew philosophy or medieval Jewish intellectual history, with evidence of potential for high-quality research; a strong publication record is highly desirable.Proficiency in Hebrew text entry, with the ability to read and interpret medieval manuscripts.Desirable:Background in digital humanities.Facility in another language in RevLog’s coverage (Latin, classical Greek, Arabic) or relevant to the study of the broader translation movement (Syriac).

GISME Junior Fellows teach two sections of an ethics course per year in either MSB or Georgetown’s philosophy department, collaborate with GISME faculty on other courses, and receive the support of Georgetown's ethics faculty to produce quality scholarship during their time in residence. new_jobs.description: The Global Commerce program at Denison University invites applications for a tenure-track position at the assistant or associate professor level beginning in Fall 2027. Global Commerce takes an interdisciplinary approach to the study of business. The program trains students to think broadly and critically about how global exchanges of goods, services, information, and money shape and are shaped by a wide variety of economic, political, cultural, social, and environmental factors. Students in the program put this training into practice through consulting projects, entrepreneurial pitches, and a variety of co-curricular experiences. The current faculty includes scholars in history, economics, anthropology, organizational behavior, English, and philosophy.We are hiring a tenure-track faculty member from the humanities or humanistic social sciences whose research focuses on questions related to business, trade, or economic life. The hire will teach across our core curriculum, which includes an introductory course on the relationship between commerce and society, an introductory course on how businesses function in the modern economy, an intermediate course centering on a local business consulting project, and an advanced global entrepreneurship capstone in which students develop a business plan. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to develop commerce-related electives aligned with their research area.  (For more details on the Global Commerce curriculum, please see:https://denison.edu/academics/global-commerce.)The teaching load is 5 courses per year, the largest of which is capped at 25 students. A PhD is required by the time of appointment. Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to excellence in liberal arts teaching at the undergraduate level, a desire to contribute to the development of the Global Commerce major, and a willingness to work with our colleagues in the Knowlton Center for Career Exploration. Applicants must also demonstrate interest in integrating global perspectives into their teaching and working in an interdisciplinary program. We will consider the extent to which each candidate’s research perspective complements those currently represented in the Department. Applicants must also provide evidence of an active research agenda; continued scholarship is required of all tenure-track and tenured members of the Denison faculty. Additional work experience in the business, government, or non-profit sectors is strongly valued as a complement to academic expertise.Full consideration will be given to applications received byOctober 30th, 2026, though we will continue to accept applications until the position is filled. We expect candidates to have their PhD in hand by August 2027.Applicants should submit the following electronic application materials on-line: (1) a cover letter that explains the candidate’s commitment to liberal arts teaching and discusses the candidate’s interest in our interdisciplinary, practically-oriented approach to the study of Global Commerce; (2) a curriculum vitae; (3) a teaching statement or portfolio that lays out the candidate's teaching philosophy, interests, and experience; (4) a 1-2 page description of the candidate’s research agenda; (5) a writing sample; and (6) a list of three academic references (upon narrowing our pool of candidates, we will ask for letters).

new_jobs.title: Associate Director of the Ethics Institute
new_jobs.description: Kent Place School, an independent, K-12, all-girls day school in Summit, NJ,  seeks an innovative and proactive Associate Director of the Ethics Institute to partner with the Director in building, implementing, and advancing groundbreaking ethics programming.Founded in 2007, the Ethics Institute at Kent Place School (EIKPS) is a first-of-its-kind program at the primary and secondary school levels. Its mission is to promote the process and practice of ethical thinking and ethical decision-making to students, parents, faculty, and staff. EIKPS helps to prepare students to be empathic citizens and the most effective leaders of tomorrow through a variety of programs, initiatives, workshops, and classes. Partnerships with institutions such as Georgetown University, Montclair State University, and Atlantic Health Systems enhance EIKPS's programs, which include “The Bioethics Project,” “Ethics and Economics“ and “Ethics in Action.”The Associate Director of the Ethics Institute is a full-time, 12-month position that serves as a primary thought leader and facilitator across the community, driving ethics initiatives, workshops, and strategic partnerships both within Kent Place School and nationallzzz zy at the primary and secondary school levels.Key ResponsibilitiesCurriculum & Program Leadership: Teach ethics courses and lead/support faculty in integrating ethics into existing coursework. Manage the creation, development, and integration of the ethics curriculum across all school divisions in collaboration with academic leaders. Oversee student publications, moderate co-curricular initiatives (such as student ethics podcasts and discussion groups), and direct summer ethics programs.Event & External Programming: Coordinate logistics and execution for signature events, including regional and national Middle School Ethics Bowls, host workshops, and deliver professional development for external organizations.Strategic Partnerships & Thought Leadership: Expand the reach and reputation of the Ethics Institute by cultivating new institutional partnerships, presenting at national conferences, and producing original blogs, newsletters, and case studies.Community Engagement: Serve on internal advisory boards, partner with parent liaisons to deliver community programming, and actively participate in school life while upholding Kent Place's mission and strategic plan.Key QualificationsEducation & Experience: Master’s degree required (with coursework or background in ethics, philosophy, or a related field) and a minimum of 5 years of teaching experience.Academic & K-12 Expertise: Deep understanding of K-12 school communities, curriculum development, and an entrepreneurial approach to expanding educational initiatives.Communication & Public Speaking: Exceptional writing, presentation, and social media skills with a proven ability to engage students, faculty, and national conference audiences.Organization & Collaboration: Strong project management skills, detail-oriented,, and the ability to manage complex multi-stakeholder programs and deadlines.The full job description can be foundhere.Kent Place School is an equal opportunity employer. We seek candidates who support the development of a school community that is culturally competent and a working environment that is affirming and inclusive, where each member feels safe and valued, as described in ourBelongingStatement.Pleasesubmita cover letter and resume to apply.

new_jobs.institution: Philosophy, Brown University
new_jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Early Modern Philosophy
new_jobs.aos: Early Modern Philosophy, Other Than Kant
new_jobs.description:
The Department of Philosophy at Brown University is looking to hire one tenure-track Assistant Professor specializing in aspects of Early Modern Philosophy other than Kant, beginning July 1, 2027. The appointee for this position is expected to maintain an active research agenda on Early Modern philosophers other than (or as well as) Kant; to teach 3 courses per academic year; to advise undergraduate and graduate students; and to perform departmental and university service. AOS: Early modern philosophy, other than Kant. AOC: OpenThe review of applications will begin on 1 November 2026. To assure full consideration applicants should submit their materials by that date. For questions regarding this position, please email[email protected].

 






QualificationsThe appointee must hold a PhD or equivalent degree or have completed all requirements for the PhD by June 2027.
new_jobs.instructions: Applicants should submit their application via interfolio https://apply.interfolio.com/194144. The application must include a cover letter, a CV, a teaching statement (and sample syllabi if available), a research statement, and a writing sample. Candidates should address in their materials (cover letter or statements) how they would contribute to the research and/or teaching missions of our diverse and inclusive university community.  Applicants should request the submission of at least three reference letters from outside Brown.

new_jobs.institution: Department of Philosophy, Miami University
new_jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor (continuing but non-tenure track)
new_jobs.job_category: Junior faculty / Tenured, continuing or permanent
new_jobs.description: AOS: Medical EthicsAOC: Applied EthicsThe Department of Philosophy at Miami University invites applications for an Assistant Teaching Professor position in Medical Ethics, with competence in other areas of applied ethics and/or environmental philosophy. We have teaching needs in applied ethics, environmental philosophy, and writing philosophy.  The College of Arts and Science at Miami University increasingly focuses on preparing students for careers in healthcare, including nursing, physician assistant, and pre-med programs.  The successful candidate will teach 12 credit hours per semester, including Medical Ethics at least once a year, and possibly every semester. The remaining teaching load would include introductory courses and other Applied Ethics courses.  Prior coursework in biology and/or the health sciences is desirable but not required. Service to the department and university is expected. The successful candidate will also work closely with the Mallory-Wilson Center for Healthcare Education.Assistant Teaching Professor positions at Miami University are non-tenure track positions, but are renewable and have opportunities for promotion (Associate and Full ranks) that include long-term contracts. We seek a candidate who will flourish in a pluralist department.Must have PhD in Philosophy by Spring 2027. Teaching experience and demonstration of teaching effectiveness required.
new_jobs.instructions: Please include CV, cover letter, statement of teaching philosophy, evidence of teaching effectiveness, and writing sample.
